simple.summary: בִּלְעֲדֵי (bilʻădêy) means except , without , besides First listed occurrence: 2Kgs 18 25.

definitions.full: H1107. bilade בִּלְעֲדֵי (perhaps from בַּל and עֲדֵי עַד, unto ; Syriac = ἄνευ , χωρίς ; Nabataean בלעד except , Eut Nab 3, 9 ) — suffix בִּלְעָדַי (3 t.), בַּלְעָדַי (4 t.), בִּלְעָדֶיךָ (once) — properly not unto , hence apart from, except, without: a. Job 34:32 אֶחֱזֶה בִּלְעֲדֵי except, apart from (what) I see myself, do thou instruct me. With suffix Gen 41:44 בִּלְעָדֶיךָ apart from thee, without thee, no one shall lift up the head, Isa 45:6 for there is none בִּלְעָדָ֑י except me. Also with suffix, as a particle of deprecation, Gen 14:24 בִּלְעָדַי not to me ! i.e. I claim nothing, (in our idiom) not at all ! 41:16 . b. with מִבַּלְעֲדֵי מִן, (so without ). ( α ) apart from , especially with the collateral idea of without the knowledge and consent, Num 5:20 ; 2Kin 18:25 ( = Isa 36:10 ) am I now come up apart from, without ׳י against this place to destroy it? Jer 44:19 (compare בִלְעָדֶיךָ Gen 41:44 ). ( β ) apart from, besides, except , Josh 22:19 ; 2Sam 22:32 a ( = Psa 18:32 a) for who is God except ׳י ? 18:32 b; similarly Isa 43:11 מוֺשִׁיעַ מִבַּלְעָדַי וְאֵין , 44:6 , 8 ; 45:21 .
definitions.rootNote: or בַּלְעֲדֵי ; constructive plural from 1077 and 5703 , not till, i.e. (as preposition or adverb)
